name: The Nature of Things
description:
The Nature of Things is a Canadian television series of documentary programs. It debuted on CBC Television on November 6, 1960. Many of the programs document nature and the effect that humans have on it. The program was one of the first to explore environmental issues, such as clear-cut logging.

The series is named after an epic poem by Roman philosopher Lucretius: "Dē Rērum Nātūrā" — On the Nature of Things.

videos.title: The Brain That Changes Itself
videos.overview: The revolutionary new understanding of the brain's functional and structural capacities.

videos.title: Visions of the Future - The Suzuki Diaries
videos.overview:
The Suzuki Diaries is a road trip, a travelogue, an adventure. The legendary David Suzuki and his youngest daughter Sarika, a university student about to start her own career in the sciences, are full of hope as they travel to Europe to see what sustainability truly looks like.

In Germany, Denmark, France and Spain, they set out to meet the people working to restore the equilibrium between human needs and planetary limits. They find a renewable energy expert, a biodynamic farmer and writer, a blogging bike enthusiast, two meticulous industrial designers, and a political powerhouse in the green movement. What they discover is that sustainability can be built into the fabric of contemporary life, not just by environmentalists but by anyone, across the full spectrum of society. The idea, innovations and inspiring individuals David and Sarika encounter prove that sustainability does not mean sacrificing quality of life.

The Suzuki Diaries illustrates what is truly possible if humans have the will.

videos.title: Visions of the Future - Supercar: Building the Car of The Future
videos.overview:
We’ve come a long way since the first “horseless carriages” began to transform not just how we get from one place to another, but also how we think about transportation, urbanization, city-planning and personal mobility in general. With rising fuel prices and growing environmental concerns, never before has it been so urgent to imagine what next year’s model might look like. But there is hope. All over the world there are people trying to figure out how to build an environmentally and socially sound version of the car.

Join engineering professor Brian Fleck on a quest to meet the engineers, designers and even students working on new technologies to make this possible. From hydrogen-powered family sedans to high end fully-electric powered sports cars, and even cars that drive themselves, you'll find plenty of surprises. Perhaps the future is not so far off as we might think — the technology that will transform our societies tomorrow is being developed today. The question is, are we ready?

videos.title: Visions of the Future - Living City: A Critical Guide
videos.overview: Despite Canada’s overwhelming urban demographic, Canadian cities struggle to provide the services expected of them, whether that means collecting garbage and fixing potholes or running schools and public transit systems. Award-winning urban affairs columnist Christopher Hume takes a cross-country journey from Halifax to Vancouver and gives the viewer a firsthand look at what’s wrong with Canada’s aging infrastructure and overall lack of political will.

videos.title: Visions of the Future - Build Green
videos.overview:
Do you remember the children's tale, "Three Little Pigs?" Build a strong house made out of bricks and mortar, and you'll be safe from the big, bad wolf. Build Green is here to show audiences that a house built from sticks and straw is better protection from the elements, and it mitigates your personal impact on global climate change.

In a refreshing hour, Build Green advises making the sun, wind and rain — along with dirt, straw and sewage — your friends. By building a house using innovative practices and materials, you'll not only do the earth a favour, but you could save big bucks too.

In Build Green, Canada's best architects hype their green creations. From retro-fitting a hip, old Montreal housing complex with state-of-the-art sustainable energy systems, to pitching hay for strawbale houses, to building transportable "mini-homes" with their own small power plant, take a close look at the materials and means we can all adopt for building green homes.

videos.title: VIsions of the Future - Earth Energy
videos.overview: Filmmaker Bill Lishman journeys around the world in search of earth’s renewable energy. He discovers Canada’s rich history of hydroelectric production, finds the world’s largest solar power plant in the Mojave Desert and makes the discovery that 25% of Denmark’s electricity is produced with wind turbines. Lishman explores North America’s wealth of renewable resources and looks at ways other countries are harnessing earth energy in clean, safe methods.

videos.title: A Murder of Crows
videos.overview: A Murder of Crows is a visually stunning one-hour documentary that offers a rare and intimate glimpse into the inner life of one of the most intelligent, playful and mischievous species on the planet - the common crow. It is also a film that explores a unique pairing of science and cinema as world-renowned scientists, including crow expert Professor John Marzluff, joins forces with an award-winning camera team to explore the secret world of crows. A scientific exploration with a compelling twist, the film is a visually stunning HD documentary that reveals new insights and understanding into this haunting and elusive species.

videos.title: The Mendi
videos.overview: It was not until 1930 that the outside world knew that there were people living in the highlands of Papua, New Guinea. In 1950 the first contact was made with a group of 55,000 Mendi, part of a million inhabitants of the New Guinea highlands, formerly not known to exist. The Australians have since built an airstrip, a hospital, schools, a hotel and other permanent buildings there, but the Mendi have kept their culture intact. A CBC film crew directed by Nancy Archibald has recorded some of the ancient culture and lifestyle of the Mendi and the results are presented in this special one-hour documentary.

videos.title: The Sexes, part 1 of 2
videos.overview: Examines male and female roles in society and presents a scientific study of the known biological facts about sex differences in humans.

videos.title: The Sexes, part 2 of 2
videos.overview: This program looks at hormonal changes during puberty, and the socially originated attitudes leading to differences between the sexes.

videos.title: Acupuncture
videos.overview: An exploration of the traditional art of healing as practiced in China.

videos.title: Think Before You Eat
videos.overview: A look at the eating habits of Canadians; food and nutrition, the so-called "Well-balanced diet" and problems of overeating are analyzed in this examination of the dangers of abundance

videos.title: Stockholm '72: Politics For Survival
videos.overview: A retrospective look at the summer 1972 World Conference on the Human Environment.

videos.title: Cities for People
videos.overview: The Nature of Things presents Cities Are For People, originally scheduled for February 19. It deals with new thinking in urban planning to make cities more livable.

videos.title: Migration: Animals in Cycle
videos.overview: A look at the migratory habits of birds and animals, with recent findings in animal studies reinforced with fascinating film footage of many species in their natural habitats.

videos.title: Old Enough
videos.overview: This half-hour film depicts obvious absurdities, in a subjective interpretation of The Limits to Growth, a 1970 MIT computer study forecasting economic, social and political collapse by no later than 2020.

videos.title: Recycling: The Garbage Ouroboros
videos.overview: A comprehensive examination of the form of pollution fast becoming public enemy number one in North America: garbage.

videos.title: Puffins, Predators And Pirates
videos.overview: This, was filmed on Great Island, off east coast of Newfoundland, site of puffins' nesting grounds in North America.

videos.title: The Club Of Rome
videos.overview: This group of thinkers, Club of Rome, thinks western society is on verge of chaos, social and political.

videos.title: Ellesmere Island
videos.overview: On Ellesmere Island, located 600 miles from North Pole, oil has been discovered. Island inhabitants, new and old, are seen in this half-hour film.

videos.title: Anybody's Child
videos.overview: Documentary about emotionally disturbed children living in a family environment as an alternative to institutional treatment.

videos.title: A Comet's Tale
videos.overview: Czech astronomer Dr. Luboš Kohoutek, discoverer of the current heavenly phenomenon Comet Kohoutek 1973 f, is among the participants in this full-hour special. Roy Bonisteel is host of the program which examines comets from a scientific viewpoint, and heavenly signs and portents of doom from psychological and historical perspectives.

videos.title: The First Inch
videos.overview: What goes on in very top layer of soil is often too small to see with naked eye. When photographed under a microscope.

videos.title: The Serious Business Of Play
videos.overview: Play is nature's method of learning about environment and about life for young. This explores our world of play and its importance for survival.

videos.title: Out Of The Mouths Of Babes
videos.overview: Little children learn languages, especially their own, with astonishing ease. Why this is so is subject of this film.

videos.title: The Joy Of Effort
videos.overview: How laws of physics are being applied to athletic endeavors, and coaches being taught how to use science rather than just "common sense" to help athletes get most out of their bodies.

videos.title: The Cree of Paint Hills
videos.overview: Documentary of the Cree inhabitants of Paint Hills, on the eastern shore of James Bay in Quebec.

videos.title: And God Created Great Whales
videos.overview: A documentary showing the behaviour of killer whales in the wild, in the waters off Vancouver Island.[194]

videos.title: Children's Hospital
videos.overview: Story of a child's stay in Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children.

videos.title: The Heimaey Eruption: Iceland 1973
videos.overview: A film on volcanic eruption off south coast of Iceland in 1973.

videos.title: Traveller From An Antique Land
videos.overview: An ancient Egyptian mummy rests at Pennsylvania University Museum far from where she had been prepared to spend eternity .

videos.title: Mind And Hand
videos.overview: What happens when a person makes a voluntary movement? Some say human behavior is involuntary.

videos.title: Frogs, Snakes and Turtles
videos.overview: Frogs, snakes and turtles play vital roles as janitors and regulators of the environment.

videos.title: Discovery on Charlton Island
videos.overview: An archeological party discovers evidence that an old Hudson's Bay site at the foot of James Bay had been burned down by the French in the 17th century.

videos.title: The First Inch
videos.overview: What goes on in the very top layer of the Earth's soil is often too small to see with the naked eye. When photographed under a microscope, that first inch of soil reveals itself to be one of the most vital of the life cycles affecting man.

videos.title: Out of the Mouths of Babes Pt. 1
videos.overview: Season Debut: A two-part film about the ease in which little children learn languages.

videos.title: Ears to Hear
videos.overview: Severely deaf children learn to speak like normal children with the aid of powerfully sensitive hearing aids and teaching techniques being used by dedicated teachers.

videos.title: Sable Island
videos.overview: A look at Sable Island, about 100 miles off Nova Scotia, where the wildlife has had an unusual evolution because it is separated from the mainland.

videos.title: Water's Edge (Part 1)
videos.overview: Unique life forms in a pond.

videos.title: Water's Edge (Part 2)
videos.overview: Visible and microscopic life at the edge of a pond.

videos.title: Prairie Grasslands
videos.overview: Documentary on prairie dogs and one colony in particular in South Dakota.

videos.title: The Differences Are Inherited
videos.overview: The fruit fly is used as the focus for a discussion of mutations, current genetic research and the relationship of this research to some of the problems suffered by humans.

videos.title: Shelter: A Question of Control
videos.overview: The program shows how psychological experiments support those who believe that community and citizen control over their own environment is essential to the well being of city dwellers.

videos.title: Noah's Park
videos.overview: The work of a group of naturalists who are attempting to create a refuge for biblical animals by restocking a park with species inhabited land in Bible times.

videos.title: The Invisible Reef
videos.overview: Through the use of micro-photography, viewers are afforded a look at the unique way in which a reef is formed through a complex system of natural recycling.

videos.title: Newborn
videos.overview: A study of the capabilities that are innate to a newborn baby in the first week after birth.

videos.title: The Mind's Eye
videos.overview: A look at the work of scientists who are exploring regions of the brain by examining its relationship to the visual system.

videos.title: Children of the Buffalo
videos.overview: A study of the Todos tribe of India, their polyandrous marriage rituals and their unusual funeral rites. The Todos spend their lives tending the buffalo and everything they do revolves around this animal.

videos.title: The Gabra
videos.overview: The Gabra is a tribe of 24,000 people who live in the harsh terrain on both sides of the Kenya-Ethiopia border. They may be the only non-Muslim, camel raising society left in the world. Their lifestyle is cruel, filled with age-old rituals and beliefs.

videos.title: When The Wind Blows
videos.overview: A look at the uses man has made of the wind, from sailboats to windmills to modern turbines for generating electricity.

videos.title: Funk Island
videos.overview: Shows some of the species of seabirds to be found on Funk Island, situated 40 miles east of Newfoundland, which is a breeding ground of more than one million seabirds, and stresses the need for their protection against man.

videos.title: The People You Never See
videos.overview: The series' 18th season starts with "The People You Never See," a report on victims of cerebral palsy.

videos.title: The Evolution Of Flight
videos.overview: Pedestrian malls, car-free zones and multipurpose subway systems are examined in a study of urban planning and urban renewal.

videos.title: The Geese Of Wascana
videos.overview: Visit to marshes of Regina where Canada Geese spend winter on open water.

videos.title: Radiation: In Sickness And In Health
Radiation: Nuclear Power
videos.overview: A look at advantages and dangers of nuclear energy, focusing special attention on problem of waste disposal.

videos.title: The Cry Of The Gull
videos.overview: The Cry of the Gull examines the effect of chemical pollutants on Lake Ontario wildlife

videos.title: Space Shuttle
videos.overview: A look at the next development in space research: establishing a space colony supporting 10,000 people in an Earth-like environment.

videos.title: Twins: And Then There Were Two
videos.overview: This is first of a two-part report which looks at both scientific and human side of twins.

videos.title: Twins: Matching Genes
videos.overview: Part two of a two-part study of twins and the research being conducted. This program shows how scientists use the phenomenon of twins to discover more about mankind in general, particularly in the field of genetics.

videos.title: When Men Play Gods
videos.overview: he creation of new organisms using a technique called recombinant DNA

videos.title: Patterns of Pain / The Gannets of Bonaventure
videos.overview: Two films featured: Patterns of Pain explores the perception of pain in our nervous systems; The Gannets of Bonaventure looks at the largest breeding colony of gannets in North America, on Bonaventure Island; and informs of threats to the colony from pollution and tourist traffic

videos.title: Evolution Update
videos.overview: Season premiere: Anthropologist Richard Leakey discusses his work in Africa, and explains the latest techniques by which scientists measure time and age of subjects.

videos.title: Clockwork Atom
videos.overview: The phenomenon of man's changing concepts of the world is explored in relation to his desire to measure time more accurately.

videos.title: This Will Do For Today
videos.overview: A series of people of varying ages, professions and experiences express their innermost feelings on subjects ranging from dateless Saturday nights to fear of death.

videos.title: Island of Monkeys
videos.overview: A study of individual development and group dynamics in a troop of rhesus monkeys in the natural observable environment of Cayo Santiago near Puerto Rico.

videos.title: The Dogon
videos.overview: The cliff-dwelling Dogon farmers and their unique culture are studied in their homeland near the Niger River in Mali.[261]

videos.title: Toward The Sun
videos.overview: The current efforts in both the United States and Canada to harness the sun as a major resource of heat and power are examined.

videos.title: Portrait Of A Market: Sololá
videos.overview: The activities of the economic and social center of Sololá, located on Lake Atitlán in Guatemala, are viewed.[263]

videos.title: Sleep (part 1 of 2)
videos.overview: Volunteers undergo an experiment at the Montefiore Sleep Lab in New York which monitors their sleeping-awakening cycles in an attempt to learn more about the body's biological time system.[264]

videos.title: Dreams (part 2 of 2)
videos.overview: Analysis of dreams is viewed at several institutions established expressly for that purpose, and those who participate in the experiments are shown as they make notations and give recollections of what they dreamed.

videos.title: Charlie
videos.overview: Canadian paleontologist Charlie Sternberg and his work in cataloguing dinosaur fossils in the Albertan Badlands are profiled.

videos.title: The Search
videos.overview: The Search follows World Health Organization medical teams on their campaign to vaccinate the against smallpox in Somalia, the world's last location where the disease survives.

videos.title: The Cajuns
videos.overview: The descendants of Nova Scotia's Acadians and their lifestyle are profiled at their adopted home, the Bayou Lafourche in southern Louisiana.

videos.title: Flying Circus of Physics / Immune System / Monarch Butterfly / Contact Lenses
videos.overview: Dr David Suzuki visits an unusual professor who conducts a Flying Circus Of Physics, examines soft contact lenses made for extended periods of use and reports on latest immunological efforts to treat severely afflicted children.

videos.title: Hypnosis / India's Sacred Cows / Ultra Sound Scanne
videos.overview: Dr. David Suzuki reports on the use of hypnosis as a medical application and the use of ultra-sound waves for X-rays, and presents the film "Sacred Cows," dealing with the importance of domestic cattle to the Indian economy.

videos.title: Madagascar: Island of the Moon
videos.overview: The island geographically separated from the rest of the African continent and populated by numerous species of plant and animal life is examined.

videos.title: Puppets / One, Two, Three, Zero / New Wave Babies
videos.overview: In Puppets, Elizabeth Crocker at the Izaak Walton Killam Hospital for Children, Halifax, is interviewed about her use of puppets to ease children into their hospital stay. The One, Two, Three, Zero segment examines possible methods of treatment for infertile couples who wish to have children.[275] In New Wave Babies, scientists Dr. Patrick Steptoe and Dr. David Bevie are interviewed about methods used in the "test tube baby" procedure.

videos.title: Contact
videos.overview: The techniques for helping autistic children developed by Barry and Suzi Kaufman to aid their own son are examined, as are their applications in a special program being conducted by a York University graduate.

videos.title: Deep Diving / Memory: Come to Think of It
videos.overview: David Suzuki goes deep-sea diving to demonstrate the psychological changes divers experience. David also investigates the mysteries of memory – how it is acquired, and how it is lost

videos.title: Arctic Oil
videos.overview: North America's last great wilderness area, Lancaster Sound in Canada's high Arctic, is now the site of oil exploration, and a unique environment rich in animal and plant life is threatened. David Suzuki and a film crew from The Nature of Things visited Lancaster Sound to find out what the future holds for this region. The material gathered from that expedition, together with interviews with several of the native peoples and with others directly concerned with what is happening in the Canadian Arctic, are presented in this program.

videos.title: Clinical Trials / Folk Medicine / Magnetic Bacteria
videos.overview: Clinical trials, folk medicine and magnetic bacteria are discussed by Dr. David Suzuki

videos.title: Left Brain, Right Brain
videos.overview: The latest techniques used in the field of neurosciences are researched to determine the functions of both halves of the human brain.

videos.title: Insects / Oyster Culture / Science Fairs
videos.overview: The survival of insects over thousands of years, the cultivation of oysters in West Africa, and Canadian science fairs on the provincial and national levels are examined by Dr. David Suzuki

videos.title: Memories From Eden
videos.overview: Special environments which zoo officials have created for the welfare of certain animals and the enjoyment of visitors are highlighted.

videos.title: Paul Jacobs and the Nuclear Gang
videos.overview: For more than twenty years a freelance American journalist named Paul Jacobs interviewed people exposed to nuclear fall-out from bomb tests in Nevada in an attempt to establish a link between such exposure and cancer. In this episode Jacobs' investigations are examined.

videos.title: Crocodile City / Spanish Galleons / World's Largest Windmill / Cement
videos.overview: This magazine edition includes four segments: a look at Lamanai (Crocodile City), built by the Maya of Belize between 400 and 300 BC, as it was being excavated by David Pendergast of the Royal Ontario Museum, assisted by other specialists and a work-force of direct descendants of the Maya; Spanish Galleons: A look at the recent discovery and exploration of Spanish treasure ships wrecked off the coast of Texas four centuries ago, and techniques used in identifying encrusted objects; World's Largest Windmill: Students and teachers of a Danish Folk School have built a windmill 75 meters high that produces 2,000 kilowatts of electricity, and Cement: A look at the properties of cement.

videos.title: High altitude Physiology / The Vision of Galileo / Dust Storms
videos.overview: Technological developments involving man's survival at high altitudes; a look at the life of Galileo, Italian astronomer, mathematician and physicist, including recreation of some of his experiments; and an examination of the global meteorological effects of Sahara dust storms

videos.title: Seal Psychology / Chiricahuas / Violins
videos.overview: Seal Psychology: A study of the ability of seals to navigate and catch fish in waters where it is too dark for the seals to see. Chiricahuas: A look at the Chiricahua mountains and their wildlife in southeast Arizona. Violins: How violins are made, including an interview with a violin maker, and footage of students at the International School of Lute Making in Cremona, Italy.

videos.title: Up Close and Personal: The Ecology of David Suzuki
videos.overview: The program is about the natural history of this invisible world: the things that float in the air around us, the microbes that live in the dish cloth on the kitchen counter, the fungi under our fingernails, and the visitors in the saucer under a house plant.

videos.title: Reefer Madness 2
videos.overview: There is a growing number of people who regard marijuana (cannabis) as a benign medicine, offering relief to people suffering from a variety of illnesses, including epilepsy, arthritis, multiple sclerosis and glaucoma as well as lessening the side effects of medications and treatments given to cancer and HIV patients. CBC Television's THE NATURE OF THINGS with David Suzuki examines the medicinal uses of marijuana.

videos.title: Look Who's Talking...How Animals Communicate
videos.overview: It is only recently that humans have become aware that animal communication is often elegant, elaborate and subtle. Understanding how other species communicate tells us a great deal about the history and evolution of our species.

videos.title: The Hidden Killer: Portrait of an Epidemic
Lost
videos.overview: We've all felt the terror of being lost - even for just a few moments. We lose our way; a child unexpectedly vanishes in the aisles of a supermarket.

videos.title: Designing for Dignity: Engineering Body Parts
Do Parents Matter?
videos.overview: How much are children influenced by their peers? The documentary Do Parents Matter? examines a controversial concept put forth by Judy Harris, a suburban grandmother and author of the explosive book, The Nurture Assumption.

videos.title: Humans: Who are We, Part 1 – The Birth of The Human Mind
videos.overview: The Birth of The Human Mind takes viewers on an amazing journey back in time, exploring the use of language, tools and how our distant ancestors came to walk. Contrary to long-accepted belief, scientists now believe that Homo sapiens did not evolve from Neanderthals, but shared the earth with them for thousands of years. Our ancestors, the Homo sapiens, are the youngest members on the human family tree, about 150,000 years old. Homo erectus goes back 1.8 million years and Neanderthals about 200,000 years.

videos.title: Humans: Who Are We?, Part 2 – The Human Invasion
videos.overview: Paleoanthropologists, linguists, archeologists and other scientists offer the latest interpretations of fossil findings and genetic studies and posit intriguing theories on how Homo sapiens became the only existing human species. Did we kill off our cousins, interbreed and merge with them, or did they just die out? It took five million years for an upright ape to evolve into an agile, quick-thinking and inventive human being. But once our ancestors emerged in Africa, were we destined to dominate the globe?

videos.title: Weather: Dragons of Chaos
videos.overview: The nature of weather is so complex that it is really a system of chaos. Weather is often benign, but occasionally the chaos spawns fierce dragons. Severe weather - violent storms, floods and droughts - is largely beyond human control, and can be cruel. Few need reminding of the 1987 tornado that killed 27 people in Edmonton, the flooding of the Saguenay region in 1996 and the Red River in 1997, and the 1998 ice storm in Quebec.

videos.title: Lost Worlds: Wild South America: Monkey Jungles
Lost Worlds: Wild South America: Amazon Jungle
Lost Worlds: Wild South America: The Mighty Amazon
videos.overview: South America is a land of extremes. It boasts the world's longest mountain chain, the Andes; the mightiest river, the Amazon; the largest rainforest, the driest desert and the richest sea.

videos.title: Lost Worlds: Wild South America: The Andes
Amanda's Choice
videos.overview: Amanda is an insightful 19-year-old from Timmins, Ontario. She has a three-year-old son and a dilemma: whether or not to be tested for the faulty gene that will bring on Alzheimer's Disease by her mid-30s, as happened with her mother and other generations in her family. It is a disease that always leads to early death.

videos.title: The Secret Life of the Crash Test Dummy
Lost Worlds: Wild South America: Penguin Shores
videos.overview: PENGUIN SHORES is part five of the magnificent six-part BBC series Lost Worlds, covering the amazingly diverse topography of South America, and its remarkable denizens. The world's longest mountain chain stretches from the tropics to the massive Patagonian Ice Sheet of sub-Antarctica. Its icy power dominates the lives of the hardy animals that dare to call it home, making living there one of nature's greatest challenges.

videos.title: Lost Worlds: Wild South America: Great Plains
videos.overview: Lost Worlds - A six-part series on the breath-taking natural world of South America takes viewers on a cross-continent grand tour - from the mighty Amazon to the spectacular Andean peaks and the world's driest desert - stopping to view the strange and wonderful array of animals, birds and other wildlife along the way. Produced by the BBC. Narrated by David Suzuki.

videos.title: The Price of Salmon
videos.overview: Salmon are considered an excellent source of nutrition. And farmed salmon provide it inexpensively. But at what cost? The Price of Salmon explores the complex issues involved with aquaculture.

videos.title: Maisin People In Papua New Guinea
Hospital at the End of the Earth
Worst Case Scenario
videos.overview: Albertans have traditionally been proud of their mighty petroleum industry. But lately, they have begun to question how that industry works. Nowhere is this shift more apparent than along the Clearwater River in Central Alberta, near Rocky Mountain House. There, residents are opposing Shell Canada's plans to drill a sour gas well in their area. The sour gas from the well could generate $10,000 a day in gross revenue, to meet today's high energy demands.

videos.title: Me, My Brain And I Unmasking The Mystery of the Conscious Mind
videos.overview: Bob thinks but doesn't feel. Christina feels but has trouble thinking. Virginia can neither think or feel as she's pulled down into a spiral of darkness that zaps her very will to survive. Kent lives within a 20-minute time span, unable to remember his past or plan for his future. Each of these people has had an injury to a part of the brain called the frontal lobes and their stories, told in Me, My Brain And I, are helping neuroscientists unravel the mystery of what makes us distinctly human.

videos.title: Warnings from the Wild
videos.overview: All over the planet, temperature increases are affecting wildlife. Some species are spreading to new areas. For others, climate change means extinction. THE NATURE OF THINGS with David Suzuki presents Warnings From The Wild, a documentary that draws together recent evidence of the effects of the biggest climatic upheaval in 10,000 years.

videos.title: Touch: The Forgotten Sense
videos.overview: A film about the amazing, but often overlooked sense of touch. The film takes us on an artistic and scientific journey from a woman who has completely lost her sense of touch, to a deaf-blind child that can understand speech through his fingers.

videos.title: Psychopaths
videos.overview: A documentary that looks at the understanding of this condition in the scientific community, and what hope there is for treatment, therapy or a cure.

videos.title: Drug Deals: The Brave New World of Prescription Drugs
videos.overview: Are our regulatory agencies doing their best to ensure drug safety? Or are they buckling to corporate pressure to market lucrative new drugs before they are adequately tested? These are questions raised in DRUG DEALS: THE BRAVE NEW WORLD OF PRESCRIPTION DRUGS.

videos.title: Bioterror
videos.overview: Since the September 11th terrorist attack on The World Trade Center, the news has been saturated with information about a new threat, bio-terrorism. But how new is it? THE NATURE OF THINGS with David Suzuki presents BIOTERROR, an exploration of the past, present and future of bio-terrorism.

videos.title: Race Against Time
videos.overview: It's an epidemic of staggering proportions. Thirty-six million people are infected with the HIV virus worldwide, with over 25 million of them in Africa. More than 21 million people have died of AIDS, nearly 17 million in Africa alone. THE NATURE OF THINGS with David Suzuki presents RACE AGAINST TIME, a film about the greatest challenge of the 21st century and the work of Canadian Stephen Lewis, the United Nations Special Envoy on HIV/AIDS in Africa.

videos.title: Return of the Peregrine
videos.overview: Adept at diving at speeds normally reserved for fighter pilots, the peregrine falcon is the fastest and most widely dispersed creature on the planet. A one-hour documentary, RETURN OF THE PEREGRINE chronicles this majestic bird of prey's journey back from the brink of extinction.

videos.title: Living Forever
videos.overview: Biologists have seen within our genes the possibility of extending human life spans to 300 years or more. In the 21st century, will scientists reach the Holy Grail? Will they find the secret of eternal youth? THE NATURE OF THINGS with David Suzuki presents LIVING FOREVER, a look at how far scientists have come in discovering the human potential for longevity.

videos.title: Genetically Modified Foods
videos.overview: In 2001 the Government of Canada approved the following genetically modified crops for food use: canola, corn, cottonseed, flax, potato, soybean, tomato, wheat, sugar beet and squash. Is enough really known about genetic engineering to ensure that genetically modified (GM) food products are safe for consumption?

videos.title: Self-Experimenters
videos.overview: Most major advances in medicine and science and are made by people who push the envelope. From morphine to cardiac surgery, we owe much to the risks taken by scientists of the past who have experimented on their own bodies to make new discoveries.

videos.title: Sex, Lies and Secrecy: Dissecting Hysterectomy
Arktika: The Russian Dream That Failed
Killed By Care: Making Medicine Safe
Apocalypse Cow: The Mad Cow Story (Part 1)
Apocalypse Cow: The Mad Cow Story (Part 2)
Passion & Fury: The Emotional Brain: Anger
Passion & Fury: The Emotional Brain: Love
Passion & Fury: The Emotional Brain: Fear
Passion & Fury: The Emotional Brain: Happiness
Origins of Human Aggression: The Other Story
Tarantula: Australia's King of Spiders
videos.overview: The hair-raising journey to discover the secret lives of these ancient crawlers. They have been roaming our planet for more than 350 million years and survived to become the giants of the spider kingdom. And they have a reputation to match – their name alone provokes fear and loathing.

videos.title: Nature Bites Back: The Case of the Sea Otter
Port Hope: A Question of Power
Everyday Einstein
videos.overview: Everyday Einstein provides a fast-paced and jazzy look at the extraordinary impact Einstein continues to have on our daily lives.

videos.title: Homo Sapiens: The Rise of Our Species (Pt.1)
videos.overview: Homo Sapiens: The Rise of Our Species will introduce you to the ultimate family tree. This story is the story of each one of us. It's the story of the birth of humanity and civilization.

videos.title: Homo Sapiens: The Rise of Our Species (Pt. 2)
videos.overview: Homo Sapiens deftly employs both docu-drama and interviews with key scientists to illuminate the remarkable story of the origins and development of our species.

videos.title: Ghosts of Futures Past: Tom Berger in the North
Blue Buddha: Lost secrets of Tibetan Medicine
videos.overview: A look at the rising interest in the ancient healing arts of traditional Tibetan medicine.

videos.title: Beetalker: The Secret World of Bees
videos.overview: Examining how bees communicate.

videos.title: Cuba: The Accidental Revolution (Pt. 1)
videos.overview: Examines Cuba's response to the food crisis created by the collapse of the Soviet Bloc in 1989.

videos.title: Cuba: The Accidental Revolution (Pt. 2)
videos.overview: In spite of the economic crisis and US embargo, the Cuban health system is an outstanding success story around the world.

videos.title: Stephen Lewis: The Man Who Couldn't Sleep
Wild Caribbean: Hurricane Hell
videos.overview: Every year the Caribbean paradise is turned into a hurricane hell. From the beginning of June until the end of November its hurricane season in the islands. With winds of over 150 mph, 5 metre storm surges and torrential rain, the destruction caused by hurricanes makes them one of the most feared forces of nature.

videos.title: Build Green
videos.overview: In a refreshing hour, Build Green advises making the sun, the wind, and the rain – along with dirt, straw, and sewage – your friends. By building a house using innovative practices and materials, you'll be doing the earth a favour too.

videos.title: Wild Caribbean: Reefs and Wrecks
videos.overview: The clear blue waters that surround the Caribbean islands are home to some of the world's most stunning underwater treasures. Coral reefs form beautiful underwater gardens visited by angels, horse eye jacks, blue tangs and stingrays.

videos.title: Wild Caribbean: Treasure Island
videos.overview: Take the island hop of your life. Discover the rich variety of islands that are the Caribbean, and what forces have shaped this violent paradise.

videos.title: Wild Caribbean: Secret Shores
videos.overview: The Caribbean is not just the islands. We explore the least known Caribbean, that area beyond the Sea. A journey along the greatest Caribbean shoreline of all, that of Central America.

videos.title: Cuttlefish – The Brainy Bunch
videos.overview: Imagine an alien with three hearts, blue blood and a doughnut shaped brain. In an instant it could become invisible, or switch on electrifying light shows. Then imagine this bizarre creature was real, and somehow connected to us.

videos.title: Mystery of the Giant Sloths Cave
videos.overview: Today's sloths rank highly among the most surprising creatures of the animal kingdom: living suspended to the Amazon rainforest's trees, they move about extremely slowly, as if from a world where time flows differently.

videos.title: The Bear Man of Kamchatka
videos.overview: Canadian bear expert Charlie Russell rescues two orphaned cubs destined for death in a squalid Russian zoo and secrets them away to his home in the remote wilds of the South Kamchatka peninsula, in the former Soviet Union.

videos.title: Living Forever: The Longevity Revolution
videos.overview: Explorer the ongoing quest to extend human life, the cutting-edge research and the latest discoveries.

videos.title: Weather Report
videos.overview: Climate change is irrevocably altering the world as we know it, challenging our sense of the future and the fundamental values of our industrial societies.

videos.title: Game Over: Conservation in Kenya
videos.overview: Explore the impact of both colonial and contemporary initiatives in Kenya and how they affect the peoples who have traditionally lived off the land.

videos.title: The Man with the Golden Cells
videos.overview: The emerging world market in living cells, where an individual's genes can be bought and sold as commodities.

videos.title: The Nature of Things Magazine
videos.overview: Witness the exciting lead up to the launch of the new High Speed One service out of St. Pancras Station, in London. A look at the Large Hadron Collider, the largest and most sophisticated machine ever constructed by science. And an interview with musician and environmentalist, Sarah Harmer.

videos.title: Climate Change I: An Uncertain Future
videos.overview: Now that climate change is an accepted, if inconvenient, truth, how are we coping? David Suzuki takes a first-hand look at how climate change is affecting Canadians where it really hurts: in their ability to make a living.

videos.title: Climate Change II: Hot Times in the City
videos.overview: Hot Times in the City takes the pulse of three major Canadian cities: Vancouver, Toronto and Halifax, as they grapple with one of the planet's greatest threats to human health: global warming.

videos.title: The Nature of Things Magazine
videos.overview: A look into the multi-billion dollar underworld of counterfeit drugs, the tale of the Lunokhod a self-propelled robot on the Moon that could be controlled from the Earth and an interview with Boston Bruins' defenseman, Andrew Ference.

videos.title: The Edge of Eden – Living with Grizzlies
The Science of the Senses: Hearing
videos.overview: In Hearing, episode one of The Science of the Senses, finding the answer to that question will take us on a journey through the ear, into the brain and right into the heart of the human psyche.

videos.title: The Science of the Senses: Touch
videos.overview: In The Science of the Senses: Touch we will take a journey through the skin, into the subcutaneous world of our sensory receptors and up into the brain as we explore the hidden language of our most essential sense.

videos.title: The Science of the Senses: Smell/Taste
videos.overview: In this episode of The Science of the Senses, we explore how smell combines with taste, somewhere in our brain, to create the perception of flavour. Most people wrongly assume that taste dominates. But what actually allows us to differentiate one food from another beyond the basics of sweet, sour, salty, savory and bitter, is the aroma.

videos.title: The Science of the Senses: Sight
videos.overview: This episode takes viewers on a fascinating tour of our visual world, from the moment light enters our eyes, to the way this information is transformed into electrical impulses and decoded by our brain - the domain of "visual perception". The act of "seeing" takes an immense amount of brainpower, more than 65% of the brain's neural pathways.

videos.title: Wild China: Heart of the Dragon
videos.overview: Explores how China's 1.3 billion people interact with their extraordinary wildlife and landscapes.

videos.title: Wild China: Shangi-La
videos.overview: Beneath billowing clouds in China's far southwest, rich jungles nestle below towering peaks and jewel-coloured birds and ancient tribes share forested valleys where wild elephants still roam.

videos.title: Wild China: The Tibetan Plateau
videos.overview: Explore the vast windswept wilderness in one of the world's most remote places - the size of Western Europe.

videos.title: Wild China: Land of the Panda
videos.overview: Travel across China's heartland where its Han people are the centre of a 5,000-year-old civilization.

videos.title: Wild China: Beyond the Great Wall
videos.overview: Warrior nomads, bizarre wildlife and extreme weather conditions are found beyond the Wall, built by China's emperors.

videos.title: Wild China: Tides of Change
videos.overview: China's coast is an area of huge contrast-from futuristic modern cities jostling traditional seaweed-thatched villages to ancient tea terraces and wild wetlands where rare animals still survive.

videos.title: Antarctic Mission: Islands at the Edge
videos.overview: The SEDNA IV sails across the Polar Front, an area where cold turbulent Antarctic waters meet warmer water from the north - one of the earth's last great refuges for wildlife.

videos.title: Antarctic Mission: Window on a Changing Climate
videos.overview: Antarctica's inhabitants are telling us that their world is changing in complex and subtle ways. The once successful colonies of diminutive Adelie penguins are declining because of increased snowfall - one of the unexpected consequences of a warmer climate.

videos.title: Antarctic Mission: The Great Ocean of Ice
videos.overview: A cold and mysterious world that is home to some of the toughest and most unusual creatures on the planet: giant ribbon worms, dragon fish, and ancient sponges.

videos.title: Antarctic Mission: The Last Continent
videos.overview: Follow mission leader Jean Lemire and his crew as they endure 17 months on the expedition to measure the threat posed by global warming in the Antarctic - a place where the Earth is particularly vulnerable.

videos.title: The Hobbit Enigma
videos.overview: One of the greatest controversies in science today: just what did scientists really find when they uncovered the tiny, human-like skeleton of a strange creature on the Indonesian island of Flores in 2003? Since the discovery was made public a bitter dispute has split the world of anthropology.

videos.title: Rodney's Robot Revolution
videos.overview: Has the time come to meet an artificially intelligent robot? Engineer and inventor Rodney Brooks thinks so. Forget about all those shiny robotic home-helpers of the past-Brooks is out to design a robot that can think for itself!

videos.title: The Adventurers: The Last Nomads
videos.overview: Linguist Ian Mackenzie has tracked the last true nomadic hunting and gathering people on earth - the Penan of Borneo. Their way of life is quickly disappearing as aggressive logging interests swallow up their forest habitat.

videos.title: The Adventurers: The Everlasting Oasis
videos.overview: University of Toronto archaeologist Tony Mills travels to the eastern desert of Egypt where he and other archaeologists have unearthed an untouched marvel: a site of over 500,000 years of uninterrupted human habitation.

videos.title: The Adventurers: A Story Told in Stone
videos.overview: Archeologist Edmundo Edwards pulls back the vines and trees of the jungle to find huge stone cities that sprawled across the interiors of Tahiti, Raivavae and the Marquesas Islands.

videos.title: The Suzuki Diaries: Europe
videos.overview: David Suzuki and his daughter Sarika head out on a road trip across Europe to see sustainability in action and meet the people who are working towards restoring the equilibrium between human needs and planetary limits.

videos.title: The Adventurers: The Lost People of Baja
videos.overview: Canadian paleo-pathologist Eldon Molto is leading the search for clues of the mysterious Pericu people of Baja California, Mexico - a fierce, primitive tribe that disappeared over a century ago, after being exposed to European disease. They left virtually nothing behind but their bones.

videos.title: The Brain that Changes Itself
videos.overview: Based on the best-selling book by Toronto psychiatrist and researcher Dr. Norman Doidge, a look at how we view the human mind.

videos.title: Gone Sideways
videos.overview: A light-hearted look at serendipity in science, from life-saving cancer cures to the x-ray machine and the discovery of North America.

videos.title: Black Wave: The Legacy of the Exxon Valdez
videos.overview: A saga about what happens when ordinary people struggle for justice against a huge corporation that has destroyed both their environment and their livelihoods.

videos.title: Supercar: Building the Car of the Future
videos.overview: Engineering professor Brian Fleck on a quest to meet the engineers, designers and even students who are trying to build the car of the future.

videos.title: Living City: A Critical Guide
videos.overview: What's wrong with Canada's cities? What's right? Award-winning urban affairs columnist Christopher Hume takes a cross-country journey to explore the sustainability, viability and liveability of Canada's population centres.

videos.title: Inuit Odyssey
videos.overview: Canadian Arctic anthropologist Niobe Thompson takes us on a visually stunning journey across the North, tracing the origins of the modern Inuit.

videos.title: American Savannah
videos.overview: Our lawns are one of our simplest pleasures. Grass is a luxury that represents relaxation, freedom, time off and of course, time away from the world of tarmac and concrete. A wild and quirky ride into the world of one of America's longest-standing obsessions, the perfect lawn.

videos.title: Arctic Meltdown: A Changing World
videos.overview: From new companies rushing to claim the Arctic's plentiful resources to the effect climate change has had on animals as well as plant life. As the Arctic meltdown continues at an ever accelerating pace, who will protect it?

videos.title: Arctic Meltdown: The Arctic Passages
videos.overview: Until recently, only a few ships braved travel through these ice-strewn waters. More and more ships cross these seas each year and with more traffic come higher risks.

videos.title: Arctic Meltdown: Adapting to Change
videos.overview: A look at two different Arctics - one that is the storybook land of ice, snow and polar bears and the other that is covered with petroleum plants and pipelines carrying fossil fuels.

videos.title: A Murder of Crows
videos.overview: A rare and intimate glimpse into the inner life of one of the most intelligent, playful and mischievous species on the planet.

videos.title: Mini Monsters of Amazonia
videos.overview: A look at the astonishing and complex relationships of the "mini monsters", insects of the Membracidae family - treehoppers that live amid one of the richest ecosystems on the planet, one so mysterious most people don't even know that it exists.

videos.title: Broken Tail's Last Journey
videos.overview: A personal quest to discover the truth behind the disappearance of a captivating tiger, one of the world's leading tiger cameramen, tracks the escape and subsequent wanderings of a male tiger, named Broken Tail, from Ranthambore National Park.

videos.title: Darwin's Brave New World: Origins
videos.overview: The extraordinary and often harrowing story of Charles Darwin's 30-year struggle to piece together the mystifying puzzle he saw in nature, and publish his theory on the evolution of life on earth.

videos.title: Darwin's Brave New World: Publish and Be Damned
Suzuki Diaries: Coastal Canada
videos.overview: A father and daughter set out with hope on a journey of discovery to Canada's three coasts determined to find solutions for a troubled ocean and look signs of a sustainable future.

videos.title: To Bee or Not to Bee
videos.overview: Could bees be an early warning sign of a larger problem with our ecology? Are they the canary in the coal mine for the health of planet earth?

videos.title: Bugs, Bones & Botany: The Science of Crime
videos.overview: Meet nature's detectives; how bugs, plants, bones ... even dust can be formidable enemies of crime.

videos.title: The Downside of High
videos.overview: Is today's strong pot damaging young minds? That provocative question is at the heart of this new documentary on recent science discoveries about marijuana and mental illness.

videos.title: Bat & Man
videos.overview: Bats are scientifically extraordinary creatures. Now scientists have begun unlocking the secrets of the bat and are developing potential medical therapies based on their discoveries.

videos.title: My Nuclear Neighbour
videos.overview: What would you do if you discovered a nuclear plant might be built right next door? Two women from Peace River Alberta journey into Ontario's nuclear heartland, to find out for themselves about life with a nuclear neighbour.

videos.title: Uakari: Secrets of the Red Monkey
videos.overview: A journey into the rainforests of the Peruvian amazon to investigate the mysterious Red Uakari monkey, never before filmed in the wild.

videos.title: One Ocean: Birth of an Ocean
videos.overview: Explore the ocean's tumultuous history and how the ocean transformed the earth into the livable, blue planet it is today.

videos.title: One Ocean: Footprints in the Sand
videos.overview: Ancient traditional fisheries, over-development and the places of recovery that can give us hope for a healthy future ocean all intersect.

videos.title: One Ocean: Mysteries of the Deep
videos.overview: Starting in the deepest part of the ocean, take a secret and magical world of bizarre creatures and new discoveries deep beneath the surface.

videos.title: One Ocean: The Changing Sea
videos.overview: Explore some of the most stunning underwater locations in the world and set sail on a scientific race to predict the fate of the global ocean.

videos.title: Masters of Space
videos.overview: Is space becoming a new war zone? A revealing look at the fine line between space-faring and space warfare.

videos.title: Aliens of the Deep Sea
videos.overview: The octopus is a close cousin of the oyster and snail. And yet, even by human standards the multi-limbed creature is considered highly intelligent. From Spain to Vancouver Island to Capri, Italy, scientists are testing the brain-power of the mysterious and mythic octopus.

videos.title: Changing Your Mind
videos.overview: Once thought to be incapable of fundamental change, our growing awareness of the adult brain's capacity for neuroplasticity is opening new doors to treatments for diseases and disorders once thought incurable.

videos.title: For the Love of Elephants
videos.overview: An intimate look at the bond that is formed between humans and baby orphaned elephants at the David Sheldrick Wildlife Trust rehabilitation centre just outside of Nairobi, Kenya.

videos.title: Geologic Journey 2: Tectonic Europe (July 8 1997)
videos.overview: Traverse the Eurasian plate across Europe — from Iceland, where new land is formed - to the Alps, where old land is destroyed.

videos.title: Geologic Journey 2: Along the African Rift (September 2, 1997)
videos.overview: For millions of years the East African Rift has been widening at the seams, tearing the African plate in two.

videos.title: Geologic Journey 2: The Western Pacific Rim (November 4, 1997)
videos.overview: Focusing on the Asia-Pacific side of The Pacific Rim of Fire, which stands as a living testament to the beauty and danger that powerful geologic forces can deliver. The Pacific Rim is home to half of the world's active volcanoes and ninety percent of the world's earthquakes, yet nearly 800 million people continue to live within its violent edge.

videos.title: Geologic Journey 2: The Pacific Rim: Americas (January 13, 1998)
videos.overview: Nick Eyles continues to explore the Pacific Rim, this time looking at the west coast of North America.

videos.title: Geologic Journey 2: The Collision Zone: Asia (March 17, 1998)
videos.overview:
The fiery unpredictability of Indonesia’s volcanoes at one end, the massive Himalayas at the other and millions of years of tectonic tension in between.

The collision zone of the old world is about to be the hub of the new. India, the Himalayas and the island arc of Indonesia - these lands will form the centre of the world’s next supercontinent.

videos.title: When North Goes South
videos.overview: Learning and discussing the consequences of magnetic pole inversion.

videos.title: Code Breakers
videos.overview: Who were the first peoples of North America? Anthropologist Niobe Thompson embarks on a voyage of scientific discovery, using the latest in DNA analysis techniques to unlock the secrets behind humanity's earliest appearance in the Americas.

videos.title: Tipping Point: The Age of the Oil Sands
videos.overview: Tipping Point: The Age of the Oil Sands is a two-hour visual tour de force, taking viewers inside the David and Goliath struggle playing out within one of the most compelling environmental issues of our time

videos.title: The Last Grizzly
videos.overview: Filmmaker Jeff Turner documents grizzly bears in the Northern Cascades of British Columbia.

videos.title: Return of the Prairie Bandit
videos.overview: Revisiting the 2009 release of nearly extinct black-footed ferrets in Saskatchewan to see what happened.

videos.title: Raccoon Nation
videos.overview: Is your garbage can making raccoons smarter? Stunning footage shot in the deep, dark of night combines with groundbreaking research in this fascinating documentary to explore the remarkable ways that city life is changing raccoons.

videos.title: The Real Avatar
videos.overview: In James Cameron's film, Avatar, an alien tribe on the distant planet of Pandora fights the human invaders bent on mining their forest home. Instead of Pandora, think Peru.

videos.title: Force of Nature: The David Suzuki Movie
videos.overview: David Suzuki, scientist, educator, broadcaster and activist, delivers what he describes as 'a last lecture' interwoven with scenes from his life and lifetime – the major social, scientific, cultural and political events of the past 70 years.

videos.title: Save My Lake
videos.overview: Save My Lake is a TV documentary episode.

videos.title: 50 Years of the Nature of Things
videos.overview: A celebration of half a century of a landmark science and natural history series, and an unrivaled Canadian institution.

videos.title: The Nano Revolution: Welcome to Nano City
The Nano Revolution: More Than Human
The Nano Revolution: Will Nano Save the Planet?
Jungle Prescription
videos.overview: One of the most powerful hallucinogenic drugs on the planet is in a tea made from medicinal plants: it's called ayahuasca. There are studies around the world that say that this indigenous cure may also provide answers as to how to treat Western drug addicts.

videos.title: Emperor's Lost Harbour
videos.overview: In Istanbul, Turkey, workers building a railway tunnel make a remarkable discovery - an ancient harbour, buried and shrouded in mystery ...until now. Will archaeologists be able to uncover the treasures of the past before it is buried again?

videos.title: Myth or Science
videos.overview: Scientist Jennifer Gardy turns her critical eye towards the myths, lies, misunderstandings and errors behind the headlines, putting the science of the daily news to the test both in the lab and on the streets.

videos.title: Waking the Green Tiger
videos.overview: Examining modern China's ideas about nature and the environment.

videos.title: Autism Enigma
videos.overview: A fresh perspective on autism research with the developing "Bacterial Theory" of autism. The fastest-growing developmental disorder in the industrialized world, autism has increased an astounding 600 per cent over the last 20 years. Science cannot say why. Some say it's triggered by environmental factors and point to another intriguing statistic: 70 per cent of kids with autism also have severe gastrointestinal symptoms. Could autism actually begin in the gut? The Autism Enigma looks at the progress of an international group of scientists who are studying the gut's amazingly diverse and powerful microbial ecosystem for clues to the baffling disorder.

videos.title: Programmed to be Fat?
videos.overview: New science links man-made chemicals to the global obesity epidemic. Man-made chemicals may be programming us to be fat - before we're even born.

videos.title: Surviving :) The Teenage Brain
videos.overview: A look at the science deep within the teenage brain and a celebration of evolution's masterpiece - the years that bring us judgment, adaptation and innovation. In short the years that make us human.

videos.title: Mysteries of the Animal Mind
videos.overview: Scientists explore the mysteries of animal consciousness and find growing evidence of compassion, cooperation, altruism, empathy, intelligence and communication in all sorts of different species.

videos.title: The American Tiger
videos.overview: Most tigers today are privately owned - experts estimate that the number of tigers living in the United States is nearly double of those in the wild. What's life like for the American tiger?

videos.title: MS Wars: Hope, Science and the Internet
videos.overview: Multiple sclerosis patients use social media to engage in an unprecedented battle with the Canadian medical establishment for access to a controversial treatment.

videos.title: Suzuki Diaries: Future City
videos.overview: In a new installment of Suzuki Diaries, David and his daughter, Sarika, set out to discover whether some of Canada's biggest cities are ready for the challenges of the future.

videos.title: Journey to the Disaster Zone
videos.overview: David Suzuki travels to the areas most affected by the tsunami on its anniversary.

videos.title: The Perfect Runner
videos.overview: Anthropologist Niobe Thompson explores the evolutionary past of humans.

videos.title: Smarty Plants
videos.overview: The secrets of plant behavior.

videos.title: Polar Bears: A Summer Odyssey
videos.overview: Shot over twelve months, this blue chip wildlife documentary tells the story a young polar bear's epic migration through the icy waters of Hudson Bay and his subsequent adventures on land, where he must spend the ice-free season. It is his first summer alone without his mother to guide and feed him. His struggle to survive is set against the biggest environmental story of our time: climate change.

videos.title: The Buffalo Wolves
videos.overview: Wolves and Buffalo follows the fortunes of one pack of wolves, the Delta Pack. Will the pups survive their first year? Will the packs alpha animals retain their pack position to breed again next year? As they try to bring down the buffalo to keep themselves and their new pups alive what will the future hold for these ancient warriors?

videos.title: Nuts About Squirrels
videos.overview: There are those of us who see squirrels as cute and fascinating, but there is also a large contingent who regard them as “tree rats” - little pests that never tire of wreaking havoc in our attics, gardens, and just about anything else that catches their fleeting fancy. So who’s right? Nuts about Squirrels reveals the secret world of the ubiquitous urban grey squirrel with squirrel robots, micro-chipped acorns and an army of citizen scientists.

videos.title: The Norse: An Arctic Mystery
videos.overview: Are we alone in the universe? We may be very close to finding out. For millennia humans studying the stars had no idea if there were any other planets in the universe, let alone ones similar enough to ours to sustain life. Now, scientists may be close to discovering Earth-like planets, using a new space telescope and a technique pioneered by two Canadian astronomers.

videos.title: Lights Out!
videos.overview: Twelve hours of light. Twelve hours of dark. For our entire history we have lived and worked in rhythm with the sun. But all that changed with the invention of artificial light. Light fixtures, computer and television screens - all of these have allowed us more time to live, work, play and shorten our nights. But at what cost? Are we putting our health at risk? We explore how the type of light we are exposed to in the hours between dusk and bedtime can play tricks on our bodies and cancel the healthful benefits naturally triggered by the absence of light.

videos.title: Zapped: The Buzz About Mosquitoes
videos.overview: People struggle to combat a blood-sucking little insect that is both delicate and deadly.

videos.title: Meet the Coywolf
videos.overview: There is a new hybrid species which is part wolf, part coyote.

videos.title: The Fruit Hunters: Evolution of Desire (Part 1 of 2)
videos.overview: The exotic world of fruit and the story of nature, commerce and obsession.

videos.title: The Fruit Hunters: Evolution of Desire (Part 2 of 2)
Billion Dollar Caribou
videos.overview: The conservation of the caribou and their environment is much-contested territory.

videos.title: The Beaver Whisperers
videos.overview: The national symbol has a new role as an ecological superhero.

videos.title: The Man Who Tweeted Earth
videos.overview: Through pictures, music and poetry, Canadian Commander Chris Hadfield brings us a view of earth from space that we’ve never seen before.

videos.title: Carpe Diem: A Fishy Tale
videos.overview: North America is under attack by a sly and wily aquatic invader. Introduced in the ‘70s for the purpose of cleaning up algae in fish ponds, the aggressive Asian carp escaped into the Mississippi river system during floods. The 50-kilogram bottom feeders have advanced north at a surprising rate, becoming a familiar sight with their frenzied and often physically threatening mass leaps into the air. Despite their fascination with this newcomer, scientists on both sides of the Canada-U.S. border agree this invader is a threat we need to take seriously.

videos.title: Ticked Off: The Mystery of Lyme Disease
videos.overview: Lyme disease, a mysterious tick-borne illness, has become one of the fastest-spreading diseases in North America. Tiny, dangerous and once uncommon, the population of ticks is growing at an alarming rate. The documentary explores how climate change has hastened the spread of the ticks and this devastating disease, one that is often misdiagnosed and mistreated, and is mired in medical controversy.

videos.title: Myth or Science 2: The Quest for Perfection
videos.overview: Dr. Jennifer Gardy is back. But this time, Dr. Gardy’s journey of scientific discovery will plumb our very hopes and dreams - our quest for self-improvement. Are raw vegetables really better for you? Can you be fat and fit? Should you ditch caffeine? Dr. Gardy puts her own body on the line in lively experiments and scientific investigations to discover whether many popular health claims are science fact or science fiction.

videos.title: Brain Magic: The Power of Placebo
videos.overview: What if each of us could make the symptoms of an illness disappear? Cast a spell so powerful it would actually heal our bodies, help us walk, or breathe better? For centuries placebos have been thought of as just fake medicine, but Brain Magic: The Power of Placebo explores the growing scientific evidence that placebos can have powerful—and real—effects on our minds and bodies.

videos.title: The Great Butterfly Hunt
videos.overview: Canadian scientist Fred Urquhart unravels the mystery of the monarch's winter home.

videos.title: How to Be a Wild Elephant
videos.overview: Orphan elephant Sities must learn how to be a wild elephant when she leaves the safety of a Kenyan sanctuary to begin her journey back to freedom.

videos.title: Secrets in the Bones - The Hunt for the Black Death Killer
videos.overview: The quest to solve a great mystery in history: Identify the Black Death killer and unlock secrets that could save millions of lives.

videos.title: Trek of the Titans
videos.overview: A rare look at the leatherback turtle as it migrates between the chilly waters off Eastern Canada and the sunny beaches of the Caribbean.

videos.title: The Allergy Fix
videos.overview: Scientists are attacking food allergies in new and inventive ways, driven by the alarming increase in the number of people, particularly children, who suffer from them – and can die from them.

videos.title: Wild Canada: The Eternal Frontier
videos.overview: A remarkable journey across Canada’s natural landscapes revealing the surprising influence early humans had on the land and its wildlife.

videos.title: Wild Canada: The Wild West
videos.overview: From the Rockies to the Pacific, western Canada has astonishing wildlife and landscapes, some of which have been influenced by early humans.

videos.title: Wild Canada: The Heartland
videos.overview: From the prairies to Canada's vast boreal forest that stretches almost from coast to coast, we reveal a huge wilderness of extremes that has been shaped over millennia by both humans and wildfires. Here pronghorn antelope, the fastest hoofed land animal on earth, still haunt the grasslands, the elusive wolverine thrives in the icy remote northern forests and beaver share their cozy lodges with grateful muskrats.

videos.title: Wild Canada: Ice Edge
videos.overview: In the country's harshest climate, the wildlife survive in the tundra of ice.

videos.title: Making Wild Canada
videos.overview: Making the incredible Wild Canada series. Meet Jeff Turner, the series director, and see stories from the field.

videos.title: Stonehenge Uncovered
videos.overview: The biggest archaeological survey ever conducted of the Stonehenge landscape finds new evidence of a lost civilization.

videos.title: Gorilla Doctors
videos.overview: Dr. Mike Cranfield looks at how he managed to be working in a Canadian veterinarian surgery to end up making house calls to some of Africa's most endangered mountain gorillas.

videos.title: Dreams of the Future
videos.overview: Dr. Jennifer Gardy tries out new technology and looks at fresh ideas of our relationships with nature.

videos.title: The Cholesterol Question
videos.overview: A investigation into whether or not Cholesterol really is the cause of heart problems.

videos.title: Decoding Desire
videos.overview: From preening peacocks to promiscuous primates, what do animals reveal about our own sexual behaviour? Explore how sexual diversity and the experience of pleasure itself may be the key to species survival.

videos.title: Chasing Snowflakes
videos.overview: Scientists are unraveling the delicate mysteries of the snowflake. And what they’re learning is amazing.

videos.title: Moose: A Year in the Life of a Twig Eater
videos.overview: Experience a calf’s first year of life as it grows up in Jasper National Park amid some of the most striking scenery on the planet.

videos.title: The Equalizer
videos.overview: Every year, athletes keep going higher, farther and faster, shattering previous world records and setting new ones. But are today’s record holders really better than those of the past? Or do modern athletes get their edge from their high tech gear? Top sports scientist Steve Haake sets off on a journey to investigate.

videos.title: Pompeii's People
videos.overview: Despite intense archaeological scrutiny, much of the ancient city of Pompeii still remains a mystery. Now a team of archaeologists, scientists, and historians are taking to uncover Pompeii's secrets.

videos.title: Destination: Mars
videos.overview: The race to get to Mars is on, seizing the imagination of the world. Every month there seems to be a new revelation.

videos.title: The Wild Canadian Year: Spring
videos.overview: The first days of spring sees Arctic fox pups take their first steps and black bear cubs learn to climb trees after the long cold days of winter.

videos.title: The Wild Canadian Year: Summer
videos.overview: Killer whales and blue sharks are on the hunt, while amorous fireflies light up the night forest with their dazzling display, as summer reveals Canada’s landscape at the peak of its splendour.

videos.title: The Wild Canadian Year: Fall
videos.overview: Fall chronicles a remarkable season of change: young northern gannets leap off perilous cliffs as chipmunks race to gather winter supplies, and prairie rattlesnakes give birth to live young.

videos.title: The Wild Canadian Year: Winter
videos.overview: Lynx hunt snowshoe hares in the boreal forest and the ancient dance between wolves and caribou on Canada's vast tundra reveal the harshest time of year when landscapes are transformed by winter.

videos.title: Making the Wild Canadian Year
videos.overview: Watch the incredible feats of endurance and technical wizardry needed to capture the sequences featured in the landmark series The Wild Canadian Year.

videos.title: Lost Secrets of the Pyramid
videos.overview: The Great Pyramid of Egypt may be humanity’s greatest achievement. It’s a skyscraper of stone built without computers or complex machinery. Now the secrets of the pyramid could finally be exposed, thanks to a series of astonishing new findings. Egyptologists are unearthing evidence across the country to reveal a story that tells of more than just how Egypt built a pyramid – they are discovering how the pyramid itself changed Egypt and the world. David Suzuki is joining the experts and scientists on the front-line who are unraveling new clues to the world’s greatest ancient mystery.

videos.title: Equus: The Story of the Horse - Origins
videos.overview: A journey around the world and back in time to discover why horses and humans make perfect partners.

videos.title: Equus: The Story of the Horse - First Riders
videos.overview: Travel back to the moment humans tamed the horse, and learn how horsepower made history.

videos.title: Equus: The Story of the Horse - Chasing the Wind
videos.overview: How did humans save the wild horse from extinction? And how did we create over four hundred specialized breeds today?

videos.title: A Day in the Life of Earth
videos.overview: From volcanoes to earthquakes & dust migration to meteorites — scientists reveal how much the Earth changes in 24 hours.

videos.title: The Real T.Rex
videos.overview: Join an investigative journey around the world to uncover the mysteries of the most famous dinosaur super-predator: the Tyrannosaurus Rex.

videos.title: The Memory Mirage
videos.overview: Can we trust what we remember about our own lives? Memory scientists say most memories are full of distortions and errors.

videos.title: Spying on Animals
videos.overview: A look at how innovations in remote unmanned cameras let us bear witness to animal behaviour 24/7 - almost anywhere on earth.

videos.title: The Genetic Revolution
videos.overview: Trailblazing scientists are making ground-breaking discoveries in the rapidly evolving world of genetic engineering.

videos.title: Stay-at-Home Animal Dads
videos.overview: From emus to penguins, meet some of the most devoted stay-at-home animal dads on the planet.

videos.title: Food for Thought
videos.overview: When it comes to diet, we swallow a lot of advice. Food for Thought sorts through the latest science to create a new recipe for health.

videos.title: The Wonder of the Northern Lights
videos.overview: The aurora borealis delights and amazes us, but we're just beginning to understand its beauty.

videos.title: She Walks with Apes
videos.overview: The epic story of three legendary women who fought to save the great apes — and inspired a generation.
